court: High Court of Judicature at Bombay
trial_court: Family Court in Petition and No. A-1567 of 2000
case_name: Arundhati Deepak Patil vs Deepak Bhaurao Patil
facts_of_case: The parties got married on 26.12.1994. The respondent took admission for Engineering Degree course after marriage. She appeared for the first and second semesters but did not appear for the third semester. The petitioner filed a petition seeking divorce under section 13(1)(ia) and (ib) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955.

legal_principles.principle: The conduct of the respondent was not of such a character and gravity so as to give rise to a reasonable apprehension in the mind of the petitioner that it will be harmful or injurious for him to live with her.
legal_principles.held: Even if it is assumed that all the aforementioned incidents did occur in the manner, as stated by the petitioner and other witnesses, still in our opinion, the conduct of the respondent was not of such a character and gravity so as to give rise to a reasonable apprehension in the mind of the petitioner that it will be harmful or injurious for him to live with her.
cited_cases: Arundhati Deepak Patil vs Deepak Bhaurao Patil on 4 August, 2008

legal_principles.principle: Parties to a marriage are supposed to bring about the union of two souls, creating a new relationship of love, affection, care and concern between the husband and wife.
legal_principles.held: Parties to a marriage, tying nuptial knot, are supposed to bring about the union of two souls. It creates a new relationship of love, affection, care and concern between the husband and wife and that it brings two families together.
cited_cases: Arundhati Deepak Patil vs Deepak Bhaurao Patil on 4 August, 2008

legal_principles.principle: The door of cruelty cannot be opened so wide otherwise divorce will have to be granted in every case for incompatibility of temperament.
legal_principles.held: Though the word 'cruelty' is not defined or it is not possible to say as to when a conduct of other spouse constitutes cruelty, the door of cruelty cannot be opened so wide otherwise divorce will have to be granted in every case for incompatibility of temperament.
cited_cases: Arundhati Deepak Patil vs Deepak Bhaurao Patil on 4 August, 2008

outcome.final_order: The marriage was dissolved by decree of divorce. The permanent custody of minor daughter Hardiki remained with the respondent-mother Arundhati Patil. The petitioner-father Deepak Patil had access to said Hardiki on 1st and 3rd Sunday of every month.
